text:
Vegas turned a game that was level on chances through the first 20 minutes into a rout. After one period the expected goals were 1.05 for SEA and 0.99 for VGK, yet the Golden Knights led 2-0 on Victor Olofsson's deflection and a Tomas Hertl power-play goal 2:56 later. Neither goal was a great look (16 and 20 percent chances), but Vegas cashed them. Mark Stone then made it 3-0 short-handed 1:43 into the second, a 17 percent snap shot, and Olofsson and Jack Eichel finished off a five-goal lead before the second period ended. Eichel's was the best chance of the night, at 26 percent.

Vegas did play the better game, just not by the margin on the scoreboard. The Golden Knights held a 3.95 to 2.58 edge in expected goals and a 60 to 48 edge in shot attempts, and the second period (1.52 to 0.43) was lopsided. By the shot-by-shot replay math, VGK deserved to win about 72 percent of the time and SEA 28. Seattle's 28 shots on goal against 27 shows how little the raw count told the story. Joey Daccord let in five goals on 2.51 expected, 2.49 goals worse than an average goalie, while Carter Hart stopped 25 of 27 and saved about half a goal above expected.

Hertl finished with two goals and two assists, Eichel one goal and three assists, and Olofsson two goals in just 10.8 minutes. Vegas also won the special-teams exchange, going 2 for 5 on the power play to Seattle's 1 for 5. Shane Wright and Jared McCann scored in the third, but at 7 and 8 percent chances those goals were no more than a late consolation, and McCann's seven shots on goal were the most of anyone.
